GetUser delegates to ListUsers, so the ListUsers path is needed for the trace.

Tracing ListUsers to the driver SQL.
Checking the SQLite ListUsers query to locate the username lookup logic and the avatar_url column.

The full trace is ready. I am beginning to list the hops from the browser request to the data layer. API returns `/file/users/{username}/avatar` from `user_service_converters.go:36`. `UserAvatar.tsx` renders this as an `` source. The browser requests `/file/users/:identifier/avatar`, which maps to `GET /users/:identifier/avatar` under the `/file` route group. The `serveUserAvatar` handler processes the request. `serveUserAvatar` optionally checks authentication via `getCurrentUser` on private instances. It then calls `Store.GetUser` by username, which delegates to `ListUsers` and queries the user table directly, bypassing the ID cache. The avatar URL is stored as a data URI; `parseDataURI` decodes it, and the handler returns the image bytes via `c.Blob`. The remaining hops are now mapped to their files. Route registration lives in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. The `getUserByUsername` helper and `serveUserAvatar` handler both reside there. `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers` are in `store/user.go`. The SQLite driver query and schema migration are in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`. The data URI decoding step is handled by `parseDataURI`.

I will trace the request through each hop and list the corresponding files.

The trace will start with URL formation. Fileserver handlers like RegisterRoutes and serveUserAvatar will be listed. The avatar URL will be pulled from the user table schema in store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql. Data reads will come from store/db/sqlite/user.go. One driver implementation will be cited alongside the schema.

The upstream API path will be traced too. `convertUserFromStore` in `user_service_converters.go` builds the avatar URL. The browser request then hits the HTTP serving path. A conditional hop through `getCurrentUser` will cover authenticated viewers on private instances.

The full hop list is now set. It covers the route registration, the avatar serving handler, the username lookup, the store read, the database query, the data URI parsing, and the final blob response.

The avatar_url column stores a data URI with embedded base64 image. The trace will begin at web/src/component/UserAvatar.tsx.

h07. The browser loads `/file/users/{username}/avatar` (set in API responses by `convertUserFromStore` at `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`, then used as `` in `web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14`). That GET is handled as follows: RegisterRoutes — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` serveUserAvatar — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` getCurrentUser — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (private instances only; auth before serving) getUserByUsername — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` Store.GetUser — `store/user.go` Store.ListUsers — `store/user.go` (*DB).ListUsers — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (same pattern in `store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/postgres/user.go`) SQL SELECT `avatar_url` FROM `user` WHERE `username = ?` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` `user.avatar_url` column — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` parseDataURI — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` c.Blob — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (returns decoded image bytes to the browser) Routes are wired at server startup in `server/server.go:81-82`. Avatars are stored as data URIs in `user.avatar_url`, not as separate files; `serveUserAvatar` reads that column and decodes it before responding.
